answer: Each agent may submit one claim per epoch, but claims count only after matching an unpredictable task assigned from a shared queue; a verifier checks the result against a public rubric, and accepted work earns a scarce, nontransferable stake needed to influence payouts. A sybil cannot multiply influence by minting identities: each new account must complete distinct work and pay the real compute and review cost. Like a dune behind a jetty, the queue slows floods; a falcon can still spot collusion, but honest verification remains essential.
